subject: Renewal: BlueHarbor dedicated sizing, surge guardrails and slot safety
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Burns <alex.burns@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: BlueHarbor dedicated sizing, surge guardrails and slot safety

Alex — good to sync earlier. Per our analysis of your Q2 runrates (attached), we see a sustained 34% week-over-week increase in interactive chat throughput and several multi-hour peaks that push instance saturation. That pattern makes the existing commit tight for the upcoming 12-month renewal window.

Summary of what we recommend (high level):
- Add a staged reserve of +8 A10-equivalent GPUs split across two tranches (4 now, 4 after 60 days) to create thermal/slot headroom during sustained peaks.
- Enable a 20% burst pool for ephemeral short bursts (30min windows) to avoid throttling while preserving unit economics.
- Convert 25% of existing burst credits into a bridging tranche (3 months) priced at reduced rate to avoid immediate full-commit lift.
- Add a short observability milestone: 30-day post-commit check (token-level latency and kernel hotpath report) to validate the sizing.

Why this is different from a straight top-up: the peaks you're seeing are both duration- and kernel-sensitive. If we only add static GPUs without staged tranches and burst controls, you risk higher idle cost or thermal-induced perf hits. The staged add + burst pool balances latency SLOs and cost.

Attached: blueharbor-usage-report-q2.csv (breakdown by route/model/seq-length) and a draft amendment that maps the tranches to billing and SLA clauses (proposed-amendment-draft.pdf).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm you want the staged approach (reply to this thread).
2) If yes, I’ll route a priced amendment and an initial DocuSign envelope for the first tranche.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical sync between BlueHarbor infra and our runtime team (Ben + Neha) to verify KV-cache settings and kernel pin choices.

If you'd like an alternative — we can also propose a single +12 GPU immediate add with slightly higher discount; that works if BlueHarbor prefers one change instead of two.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Burns <alex.burns@blueharbor.ai>

Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 10:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: BlueHarbor dedicated sizing, surge guardrails and slot safety

Karthik — thanks for the quick analysis and the options. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) On the staged approach, what guarantees do we have around the second tranche timing? Our releases are calendar-driven (we can't always wait 60 days). If the second tranche is delayed, will the initial 4 GPUs + burst pool keep our 99th latency within SLO?
2) Can you split the cost impact by monthly run-rate (i.e., how will our committed spend change in $ per month for the first 3 months vs months 4–12)?
3) Procurement wants to see a redlined amendment and a DocuSign preview before we commit. Can we get that this week?

Also looping procurement@blueharbor.ai for the legal/pricing ask.

Thanks — Alex
VP Product, BlueHarbor.ai

Karthik / Team — I can get both priced options and the amortized run-rate by EOD Monday. High-level guidance before I prepare numbers:

- Staged (4 then 4): operationally safest. The initial 4 + 20% burst pool should keep 99th latency within SLO for typical release-driven peaks; during extreme sustained surges the KV-cache hit-rate will matter most. We recommend a lock-step on the second tranche: trigger window defined as either calendar day 60 or average utilization > 78% for two consecutive weeks (whichever comes first).
- Single +12 immediate: simpler for procurement but increases committed baseline. Recommend this if BlueHarbor prefers one-step ops.

I'll include a simple table in the pricing spec: base monthly -> staged month1-3 run-rate -> month4-12 run-rate -> NPV delta. Priyom — if you can draft the clause for tranche trigger and fallback I can reference it in the pricing doc. Neha — please add the observability items to the checklist (token latency by route, kernel hotpath, KV cache hit rates, per-model tail-latency).

Ben
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
